_meta.name: AlmiOET corridor proof batch — v2 (nursing → UK, 4 origins), ENRICHED + CITED
_meta.purpose: Enrich the 4 corridors ~4x with REAL, CITED origin facts so each clears the quality gate on real content (not padding). Built search-first: origin regulator + verification route + attestation chain + English-route nuance + local wording. Destination (NMC) facts are SHARED — linked once from the destination page, NOT repeated per corridor (law #3).
_meta.CORRECTION_1_english_exemption: v1 claimed Nigeria & Philippines nurses are EXEMPT from OET/IELTS via English-medium training, while Pakistan & India are not. That binary is INCORRECT per the NMC's own guidance. NONE of the four countries is on the NMC's list of 34 majority-English-speaking countries. For all four, the 'taught and examined in English' (aka 'qualified in English') route EXISTS but is CONDITIONAL: it requires (a) a training transcript/institution letter showing the course was taught AND examined in English, AND (b) supporting information from a UK employer (SIFE) — which in practice needs ~12 months already working in the UK. So a nurse applying FROM the home country, before a UK job, almost always STILL sits OET or IELTS. The genuine per-corridor English nuance is only that Philippine and Nigerian pre-registration nursing is English-medium (meets part (a) cleanly), whereas Pakistan/India medium is more variable — but the automatic exemption does NOT exist for any of them. verifyStatus: confirm-official on all English-route facts.
_meta.CORRECTION_2_philippines_apostille: v1 said 'red-ribbon/apostille'. The Philippine DFA red ribbon was ABOLISHED; the Philippines acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 14 May 2019; embassies stopped red ribbons 15 June 2019). Authentication is now by APOSTILLE only. Fixed in v2.
_meta.method: 4 independent research passes, official primary sources preferred (NMC, PNMC, NMCN, INC/state councils, PRC, DFA). Every fact carries sourceUrl + sourceName + confidence (official|secondary|notFound) + asOf. Nothing invented; unfilled slots stay notFound. Churny/interpretation facts carry verifyStatus:confirm-official and render but noindex until confirmed (currency gate).

testOfCompetence.value: Overseas-trained nurses must pass the NMC Test of Competence: Part 1 CBT (computer-based test — Part A numeracy, Part B clinical; can be taken in-country) and Part 2 OSCE (objective structured clinical examination, taken at a UK test centre). Both parts within two years of each other.

englishAcceptedTests.value: NMC accepts IELTS Academic (L7 R7 S7, W6.5) or OET (L/R/S grade B, W grade C+). Two sittings of the SAME test can be combined if within 12 months of each other. Cannot mix IELTS with OET. CEFR C1 standard.

nmcFees.value: NMC fee components (subject to change — verify current amounts): qualification/eligibility evaluation £140 (non-refundable), CBT £83, OSCE £794, initial registration £153.
nmcFees.sourceName: NMC — Information for internationally trained applicants

englishMajorityCountryList.value: The NMC's 'recent practice in a majority-English country' and automatic-exemption routes rely on a published list of 34 majority-English-speaking territories. None of Pakistan, Nigeria, India or the Philippines is on it — so none of these four gets an automatic English exemption.

sharedDestination.visa: UK Health and Care Worker visa (route broadly common across origins).

originRegulator.value: Pakistan Nursing & Midwifery Council (PNMC) — reconstituted/renamed from the former Pakistan Nursing Council (PNC).
originRegulator.note: Confirm current legally operative name/portal — pnmc.gov.pk uses the new name; older pnc.org.pk still resolves.

verificationRoute.value: Verification of registration / good standing is obtained directly from PNMC: submit the verification application form, processing fee PKR 10,000, a request letter from the receiving regulator (the UK NMC) with full contact details, and photocopies of the PNMC registration card plus all nursing/midwifery diplomas and degrees. Queries go to the Good Standing Cell (gsc@pnmc.gov.pk) with name, CNIC and PNMC registration number; stated response ~3 working days. This is a manual/email-based process, not a self-service outbound portal.

attestationChain.value: Degree attestation via the Higher Education Commission (HEC); school/intermediate certificates countersigned by the IBCC; then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Pakistan acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 9 March 2023), so MOFA now issues Apostilles (apostille.mofa.gov.pk) — HEC (and IBCC for school docs) verification remains the prerequisite step before the MOFA apostille.
attestationChain.sourceName: HCCH — Pakistan accedes to Apostille Convention

englishRoute.value: Pakistan is NOT on the NMC majority-English list, so no automatic exemption. The 'taught and examined in English' route is available but conditional: needs a transcript/institution letter (taught AND examined in English) PLUS UK-employer supporting information (SIFE). Pakistani nursing medium of instruction is variable, so most Pakistani nurses evidence English via OET or IELTS.

corridors.originDistinctSummary: PNMC email/Good-Standing-Cell verification + PKR 10,000 fee + HEC/IBCC→MOFA apostille (Hague since Mar 2023) + English via OET/IELTS in practice.

originRegulator.value: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN). Main site nmcn.gov.ng; applicant portal myportal.nmcn.gov.ng; verification info nmcn.gov.ng/verify.html. Payments via REMITA.

verificationRoute.value: The nurse uses NMCN's 'Verification of Certificate' service: apply online on the Council's portal, upload a scanned Certificate(s) of Registration and a passport photo, complete the verification form (stating destination = UK NMC), pay via REMITA. Only Certificate(s) of Registration are accepted (not exam-result/notification docs). NMCN sends the verification directly to the destination regulator.

verificationEligibilityFeesTimeline.value: Revised NMCN verification guidelines (reported effective 1 March 2024): typically a minimum ~2 years post-qualification experience and an active practising licence; NMCN contacts the training institution and workplace directly; allow ~6 months. Fees (via REMITA) reported around: standard verification ≈₦66,875, a UK-specific verification line ≈₦17,500, authentication ≈₦8,750, Letter of Good Standing ≈₦8,750.

englishRoute.value: Nigerian pre-registration nursing IS taught and examined in English (meets part (a) of the 'qualified in English' route cleanly). BUT Nigeria is NOT on the NMC majority-English list, so the transcript alone is NOT sufficient — the NMC also requires UK-employer supporting information (SIFE), which generally needs ~12 months already working in the UK. So a nurse applying FROM Nigeria (first-time registration + visa) almost always still needs OET or IELTS. The common belief that Nigerian nurses skip IELTS/OET is a misconception.

corridors.originDistinctSummary: NMCN online portal + REMITA + UK-specific verification line, ~2yr experience + active licence, ~6-month timeline, NMCN posts verification directly; English-medium training but SIFE still required so OET/IELTS in practice.

originRegulator.value: Indian Nursing Council (INC) sets national standards and runs the national live register (NRTS), but individual registration is held at the STATE Nursing Council level (constituted under the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947).

verificationRoute.value: India-distinct federal wrinkle: verification of registration / good standing for going abroad is issued by the STATE Nursing Council of first registration (e.g. Tamil Nadu TNMC, Kerala KNMC, Karnataka KSNC, Delhi DNC, Maharashtra MNC) — NOT the Indian Nursing Council. The state council completes its section of the destination regulator's verification form and sends/couriers it directly to that regulator (e.g. the UK NMC); the applicant supplies passport, registration certificate, experience proof and the destination authority's courier address. The INC sets national standards and runs the national register (NRTS) but does not issue foreign verification. Some councils (e.g. Karnataka) include a video verification appointment.

attestationChain.value: For Indian nursing/educational documents used in the UK: the document is authenticated at the State level (Home Department / HRD / SDM as applicable), then APOSTILLED by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). Because both India and the UK are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, an MEA apostille needs no further UK embassy legalisation. State nursing-council verification is a separate credential step from document apostille.

originRegulator.value: Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), acting through the Professional Regulatory Board of Nursing. PRC issues the Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card (PIC), and provides certification/authentication and stateboard verification services. Online system: LERIS.

verificationRoute.value: Filipino nurse obtains PRC-authenticated documents via LERIS: log in, book an appointment and pay, present the system-generated Action Sheet plus requirements (valid PIC/e-PIC, originals, one Documentary Stamp Tax per copy). PRC also lists a 'Stateboard Verification / Validation of Registration/License' service used by professionals going abroad. Note: the PRC page does not itself describe a direct electronic transmission to the UK NMC; third-party credential-verifiers (e.g. TruMerit/CGFNS, DataFlow) are typically used to confirm authenticity — confirm the exact PRC→NMC handoff.

attestationChain.value: CORRECTED (v1 said red ribbon): the Philippines abolished the DFA 'red ribbon' and acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 14 May 2019; embassies stopped red ribbons 15 June 2019). Documents are now APOSTILLED by the DFA: regular PHP 100 (~5 working days) or expedited PHP 200 (~2 working days); appointments at appointment.apostille.gov.ph. Because the UK is an Apostille state, an apostilled Philippine document needs no further UK legalisation.
attestationChain.sourceName: Philippine DFA — PH does away with red ribbons

englishRoute.value: Philippine pre-registration nursing IS taught and examined in English (meets part (a) cleanly). But the Philippines is NOT on the NMC majority-English list, so the transcript alone is not sufficient — the NMC also requires UK-employer supporting information (SIFE). So applying from the Philippines before a UK job, most Filipino nurses still sit OET or IELTS. Route availability is confirm-official.
